mainTopic: The verses that forbid a סוטה, two sources for doubtful טומאה, and a קל וחומר for a third-level loaf.
overview: The amud opens by finishing the argument between רבי עקיבא and רבי ישמעאל about what the word ונטמאה forbids for a סוטה. The גמרא rejects one explanation, then says רבי עקיבא has four verses: husband, בועל, כהונה and תרומה. רבי ישמעאל has three verses and learns כהונה through a קל וחומר. The גמרא explains why רבי ישמעאל uses his verse for תרומה: like the husband and בועל, תרומה matters while the husband is alive. It then gives two ways to explain רבי עקיבא. Next, רב גידל in the name of רב brings a verse as a second source for doubtful טומאה. It teaches that something that can be asked is impure when in doubt, and something that cannot be asked is pure. The גמרא shows why both this verse and the lesson from סוטה are needed. Finally it turns to the משנה about a third-level loaf. רב explains רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's view with a קל וחומר from a טבול יום. That קל וחומר is refuted, and a new source for it begins at the end of the amud and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: If a doubtful זונה counts as a real זונה, תרומה wouldn't need a verse either
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes a line of reasoning from the previous page and shows that the same logic would make the תרומה verse unnecessary too.
steps.simpleTranslation: …since the Torah treated her, a doubtful זונה, like a definite זונה. But then תרומה should not need a verse either, since the Torah treated a doubtful זונה like a definite זונה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a sentence from the previous page: maybe כהונה needs no verse, because a סוטה is treated like a real זונה. Then it pushes back: the same logic would mean תרומה needs no verse either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A real זונה may not marry a כהן and may not eat תרומה. So if a ספק זונה is treated exactly like a real זונה, both rules should follow on their own. That proves too much, because a verse for תרומה clearly exists, so this way of explaining רבי עקיבא must be dropped.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who may have been with a forbidden man, but we are not sure
A woman who had relations forbidden to her by the Torah; she may not marry a כהן or eat תרומה
The portion of produce given to כהנים, which only they and their households may eat
A verse should not be needed

steps.confusionAlert: The first half of this step is not a new idea. It is the end of a sentence that began on the previous page. The real challenge starts at the word תרומה.

phrases.english: since [the Torah] has made her
phrases.notes: This finishes a sentence from the previous page arguing that כהונה needs no verse of its own.

phrases.english: a doubtful zonah like a definite zonah.
Then teruma too should not need a verse,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהֲרֵי עָשָׂה בָּהּ סְפֵק זוֹנָה כְּזוֹנָה!
phrases.english: since [the Torah] made her, a doubtful zonah, like a definite zonah!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes and then knocks down a suggestion from the previous page about why רבי עקיבא would not need a verse for כהונה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that כהונה needs no verse because a ספק זונה counts as a real זונה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The logic proves too much. It would also make the תרומה verse unnecessary, yet that verse exists.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא has four verses: husband, בועל, כהונה, תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רבי עקיבא counts four teachings, so each prohibition gets its own verse.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, according to רבי עקיבא four verses are written: one for the husband, one for the בועל, one for כהונה and one for תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the failed explanation and gives a new one. רבי עקיבא counts four verses, so each of the four prohibitions has its own verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבי עקיבא has enough verses for all four rules, nothing has to be learned through logic. That is why he has a separate verse for כהונה even though a קל וחומר might be possible. The extra count comes from expounding the letter ו in ונטמאה.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; drops the earlier idea and brings a new one
The man she was secluded with (the suspected lover)

phrases.english: Rather, according to Rabbi Akiva,
four verses are written:
phrases.notes: These are the times ונטמאה appears in the סוטה section, plus the extra letter ו, which רבי עקיבא counts as one more teaching.

phrases.english: one for the husband, and one for the paramour,
and one for the priesthood, and one for teruma.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אַרְבְּעָה קְרָאֵי כְּתִיבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the explanation that step 1 knocked down.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Counting the verses: רבי עקיבא has enough verses that each rule gets its own.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רבי עקיבא's כהונה verse needed a special reason, such as ספק זונה logic.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי עקיבא simply has four verses, one for each of the four prohibitions.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל has three verses, and כהונה comes from a קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל counts only three verses: husband, בועל and תרומה. He learns כהונה through a קל וחומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי ישמעאל: three verses are written. One is for the husband, one for the בועל, one for תרומה, and כהונה is learned through a קל וחומר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now sets out רבי ישמעאל's count. He has only three verses, so one rule, כהונה, must be learned through logic instead of a verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל does not expound the extra ו, so he has one verse fewer than רבי עקיבא. He uses the קל וחומר from the ברייתא for כהונה: a גרושה may eat תרומה yet may not marry a כהן. So a סוטה, who may not even eat תרומה, should surely not marry a כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: An argument from a lighter case to a stricter one

steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא: four verses (husband, בועל, כהונה, תרומה). רבי ישמעאל: three verses (husband, בועל, תרומה), and כהונה comes from a קל וחומר.

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Yishmael,
three verses are written:
one for the husband, and one for the paramour,
and one for teruma,
and the priesthood is learned through a kal vachomer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the picture by setting רבי ישמעאל's count beside רבי עקיבא's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי ישמעאל uses three verses (husband, בועל, תרומה) and learns כהונה through a קל וחומר.

steps.title: Why should רבי ישמעאל's verse go to תרומה and not to כהונה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי ישמעאל uses the verse for תרומה. Perhaps it teaches כהונה instead, and a סוטה would then be allowed to eat תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי ישמעאל: how do we know the verse is needed for תרומה, with כהונה coming from a קל וחומר? Perhaps the verse is needed for כהונה, and תרומה is permitted!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי ישמעאל. It asks why the third verse must be for תרומה, when perhaps it is for כהונה and תרומה stays permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר for כהונה only works if we already know she is forbidden to eat תרומה. If the verse taught כהונה instead, there would be no source at all for forbidding תרומה. So the גמרא wants to know what forces the verse to go to תרומה. This question sets up the answer that comes next.

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Yishmael, from where [do we know]
that the verse was needed for teruma,
and the priesthood is learned through a kal vachomer?
Perhaps when it was needed, it was for the priesthood,
and teruma is permitted [to her]!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל, מִמַּאי דְּאִיצְטְרִיךְ קְרָא לִתְרוּמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the way רבי ישמעאל assigns his verses, as laid out in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ישמעאל's choice to use the verse for תרומה and learn כהונה through a קל וחומר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Nothing so far forces this choice. The verse could just as well teach כהונה, and then תרומה would be permitted to her.

steps.title: The extra verse should match the husband and paramour, which apply during the husband's lifetime
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל reads the verse as teaching תרומה, since תרומה, like the husband and בועל prohibitions, applies while the husband is still alive. כהונה only matters after his death.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל could say: it makes more sense to learn a prohibition similar to the husband and the בועל. Just as those apply during the husband's lifetime, so too the תרומה prohibition applies during his lifetime. This leaves out כהונה, which only matters after his death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 4: why does רבי ישמעאל say the verse teaches תרומה and not כהונה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband and בועל prohibitions both apply right now, while the husband is alive. תרומה also applies right now. Marrying a כהן only becomes relevant after the husband dies, so it does not fit the pattern, and רבי ישמעאל learns it through the קל וחומר instead.

keyTerms.meaning: It is reasonable / it makes sense

phrases.english: He could say to you:
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבי ישמעאל, answering the question from the last step.

phrases.english: It is reasonable [to learn something] similar to husband and paramour.
Just as husband and paramour apply during the lifetime,
so too תרומה also applies during the lifetime,
to exclude priesthood, which is after death.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ: מִסְתַּבְּרָא דּוּמְיָא דְּבַעַל וּבוֹעֵל
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reasoned reading: the verse should teach a prohibition parallel to the neighboring ones.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The verse could teach כהונה, leaving תרומה permitted.
steps.terutzMaskana: The verse teaches תרומה, which applies during the husband's lifetime like husband and בועל. כהונה comes from the קל וחומר.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא does not accept the comparison to husband and paramour
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי עקיבא would deal with this reasoning, and answers that he does not accept the comparison.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי עקיבא? He does not hold that the verse must be similar to husband and בועל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי עקיבא doesn't use רבי ישמעאל's reasoning, and gives a first answer: he simply doesn't accept it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If you don't compare the extra verse to husband and בועל, there is no reason to prefer תרומה over כהונה. So you cannot learn one of them from the other, and each needs its own verse. That fits רבי עקיבא's count of four teachings.

keyTerms.meaning: The man she was secluded with (the paramour)
He does not hold of it

phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva?
He does not hold of 'similar to husband and paramour.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, דּוּמְיָא דְּבַעַל וּבוֹעֵל לֵית לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from רבי ישמעאל's reasoning to explain why רבי עקיבא does not follow it.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects the premise: רבי עקיבא denies the comparison.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי עקיבא should also reason that the verse means תרומה and learn כהונה by קל וחומר.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי עקיבא doesn't accept the comparison, so he needs separate verses for תרומה and כהונה.

steps.title: The Torah sometimes writes out what a קל וחומר could teach
steps.stepSummary: A second answer for רבי עקיבא: even if he accepts the comparison, the Torah sometimes writes a verse for something you could learn by קל וחומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or else he does accept the comparison. But for something that could be learned by a קל וחומר, the verse went to the trouble and wrote it anyway.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another way to explain רבי עקיבא. Maybe he agrees with the reasoning but still counts both verses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here רבי עקיבא agrees that כהונה could be learned through a קל וחומר. He just holds that the Torah sometimes spells out such a law anyway. So a verse for כהונה is not a problem, even though logic alone could have taught it.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי ישמעאל: the extra verse teaches תרומה, and כהונה comes from a קל וחומר. רבי עקיבא: either he rejects the comparison, or he holds the Torah may write out a קל וחומר anyway.

phrases.english: Or alternatively, he does hold of it,
a matter that could come through a קל וחומר,
the verse took the trouble and wrote it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי נָמֵי אִית לֵיהּ, מִילְּתָא דְּאָתְיָא בְּקַל וְחוֹמֶר טָרַח וְכָתֵב לַהּ קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer for רבי עקיבא in place of step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternative answer: a principle about how the Torah writes verses.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If רבי עקיבא accepts the comparison, a separate verse for כהונה would be extra.
steps.terutzMaskana: The Torah sometimes writes a verse even when a קל וחומר could teach the law, so the extra verse is fine.

steps.title: רב's source for doubtful impurity: only certain impurity may not be eaten
steps.stepSummary: רב גידל in the name of רב gives a verse as the source for the rule about doubtful טומאה cases, split by whether the thing involved can be asked. The verse implies that only certain טומאה forbids eating.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב גידל said in the name of רב: the rule for something that has the understanding to be asked, and something that does not, comes from this verse: 'And the flesh that touches any impure thing shall not be eaten.' Only certain impurity may not be eaten. But if it is doubtful whether it is impure or pure, it may be eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on from the תרומה/כהונה question to another source for doubtful טומאה. The ברייתא learned this rule from סוטה, and now רב gives a second source from a verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule depends on whether the thing involved can be asked about what happened. רב reads the verse closely: it forbids flesh that touched something טמא. That suggests a case of certain טומאה is forbidden, while a doubtful case may be eaten.

keyTerms.meaning: Understanding to be asked (able to answer questions about what happened)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a source for the rules of ספק טומאה, which the גמרא will keep working on.

phrases.english: Rav Giddel said that Rav said:
Something that has the understanding to be asked
and something that lacks the understanding to be asked
is derived from this verse:

phrases.aramaic: ״וְהַבָּשָׂר אֲשֶׁר יִגַּע בְּכׇל טָמֵא לֹא יֵאָכֵל״;
phrases.english: "And the flesh that touches any impure thing shall not be eaten";
certainly impure is what shall not be eaten,

phrases.aramaic: הָא סָפֵק טָמֵא וְסָפֵק טָהוֹר — יֵאָכֵל.
phrases.english: but if it is uncertain whether impure or pure, it may be eaten.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב גִּידֵּל אָמַר רַב: דָּבָר שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ דַּעַת לִישָּׁאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the תרומה/כהונה discussion and brings a second source, from a verse, for the doubtful-טומאה rule that the ברייתא learned from סוטה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The verse 'והבשר אשר יגע בכל טמא לא יאכל' is the source for the rules on doubtful טומאה. Read simply, only certain טומאה forbids eating, and a doubtful case may be eaten.

steps.title: The end of the verse seems to say the opposite
steps.stepSummary: The second half of the same verse implies that a person who is only possibly impure may not eat קדשים meat. This clashes with the first half, which treated a doubt as pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Look at the end of the verse: 'And as for the flesh, every one that is pure may eat the flesh.' This means only someone who is definitely pure may eat. But someone who might be impure and might be pure may not eat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points to the second half of the same verse. That half seems to say that a doubt about טומאה makes you impure, which is the opposite of what the first half implied.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 8, the first half ('meat that touches anything impure') suggested that only definite טומאה forbids eating, so a doubt stays pure. The second half ('every one that is pure may eat') suggests that only definite purity allows eating, so a doubt is impure. The two halves of one verse now seem to contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: Say the end part (of the verse)
Maybe impure and maybe pure, a case of doubt

phrases.english: Say the latter clause:
"And as for the flesh, every one that is pure
may eat the flesh";
it is one who is certainly pure who may eat meat,
but one who is possibly impure and possibly pure
may not eat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading from step 8 by using the second half of the same verse
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference from the first half of the verse that a doubt about טומאה is pure
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The second half implies that only definite purity allows eating, so a doubt would be impure. That contradicts the first half.

steps.title: Two kinds of doubt: something that can be asked and something that cannot
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא resolves the contradiction. The verse is teaching two different rules for two different kinds of cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: So we must learn from this: one half of the verse is about something that has the awareness to be asked. The other half is about something that does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction by saying each half of the verse speaks about a different kind of case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person who is unsure whether he became impure can be asked, and his doubt counts as impure. That is the second half, 'every one that is pure.' Meat or an object cannot be asked, so its doubt counts as pure. That is the first half. So there is no contradiction, and this is exactly the split רב's source was meant to show.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, must we not learn from it
It has awareness to be asked (a person)
It has no awareness to be asked (an object or animal)

steps.whatToRemember: With a doubt about טומאה, something that can be asked (a person) is treated as impure. Something that cannot be asked (an object) is treated as pure.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basic dividing line for doubts about טומאה, and it is the main source רב גידל was teaching.

phrases.english: Rather, must we not conclude from it:
here, where it has awareness to be asked,
phrases.notes: This is the person in the second half of the verse, 'every one that is pure.'

phrases.english: there, where it has no awareness to be asked.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 9
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each half of the verse covers a different kind of case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two halves of the verse contradict each other about doubtful טומאה
steps.terutzMaskana: Something that can be asked is impure when in doubt. Something that cannot be asked is pure when in doubt.

steps.title: Why the source from סוטה is still needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says both sources are needed. With only רב's verse, we would think the rule applies in a public domain too. סוטה teaches that it applies only in a private domain.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both רב גידל's teaching in the name of רב and the lesson from סוטה were needed. If we had only רב's source, I would have said the rule applies both in a private domain and in a public domain. So we needed to learn from סוטה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to explain why we need two sources for doubts about טומאה. Here it gives the reason the סוטה source is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's verse only tells us that a person who can be asked is impure when in doubt. It says nothing about where the doubt happened, so we might apply it everywhere. סוטה involves being secluded in private, so learning from her limits the rule to a private domain.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have said (a mistaken first thought)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think one source made the other unnecessary. The גמרא is showing that each source adds a detail the other one lacks.

phrases.english: And the teaching of רב גידל in the name of רב was needed,
and it was also needed to learn it from סוטה.
phrases.notes: This refers to the earlier lesson on the daf, learned from סוטה, that a doubt in a private domain counts as impure.

phrases.english: For if we had only רב's source, I would have said

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין בִּרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד וּבֵין בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים,
phrases.english: that it applies both in a private domain and in a public domain,
so it was needed to learn from סוטה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיצְטְרִיךְ דְּרַב גִּידֵּל אָמַר רַב, וְאִיצְטְרִיךְ לְמִיגְמַר מִסּוֹטָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that רב's source is settled, the גמרא explains why the earlier source from סוטה is still needed
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Without סוטה we would apply the rule in a public domain too. סוטה limits it to a private domain.

steps.title: Why רב's source is still needed
steps.stepSummary: With only the סוטה source, we would think a doubt counts as impure only when both sides can be asked. רב's verse shows that one side being able to be asked is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if we had only the lesson from סוטה, I would have said the doubt counts as impure only when both the one who touches and the one who causes the touching have awareness. So both sources were needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes explaining why both sources are needed. Here it shows what רב's source adds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In סוטה, both the woman and the man have awareness and can be asked. So from סוטה alone we might demand awareness on both sides. רב's verse speaks of a person who can be asked even when the impure thing cannot, so one side being able to be asked is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who touches and the one who causes the touching
It was needed (both sources are necessary)

steps.whatToRemember: Both sources are needed. סוטה teaches that the rule applies only in a private domain. רב's verse teaches that only the person who might have become impure needs to have awareness.

phrases.english: And if we had only the lesson from סוטה, I would have said
that it is impure only when there is awareness
in both the one who touches and the one who causes the touching,
so both were needed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the explanation from step 11 by showing what רב's source adds
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both sources are necessary. סוטה limits the rule to a private domain, and רב's verse shows that awareness is needed only in the person who touches.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about רבי עקיבא's teaching on the earthen vessel
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the line of the משנה where רבי עקיבא learns from the verse about an earthen vessel that a second-level loaf can create third-level impurity.
steps.simpleTranslation: On that same day רבי עקיבא explained the verse: "And every earthen vessel..." and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is opening a new topic by quoting a line from the משנה. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי עקיבא reads the word "יטמא" ("shall be impure") in the verse to teach that a loaf at the second level (שני) makes something it touches impure at the third level (שלישי). The משנה also says that רבן יוחנן בן זכאי expected a later generation to call such a third-level loaf pure, since no verse says it is impure. The גמרא will focus on that point.

keyTerms.meaning: Explained or drew a teaching out of a verse
"Etc.": the quote continues in the source

phrases.english: On that day Rabbi Akiva expounded
"And every earthen vessel," etc.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 11:33. The 'etc.' means the rest of the משנה is assumed here, including the line about רבן יוחנן בן זכאי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of doubtful טומאה from steps 8-12 and opens a new line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא derives from the verse that a שני loaf can make תרומה a שלישי.

steps.title: If there is no verse, why did רבן יוחנן בן זכאי call the loaf impure?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if רבן יוחנן בן זכאי admitted there is no verse for the third-level loaf, why did he himself treat it as impure?
steps.simpleTranslation: And since it has no verse, why is it impure?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a difficulty with רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's view. He said there is no verse for the third-level loaf, yet he still ruled it impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It sounds self-contradictory: no source in the Torah, yet a ruling of טומאה. The גמרא wants to know what his ruling was based on.

phrases.english: And since it has no [verse],
why is it impure?
phrases.notes: He means: why did רבן יוחנן בן זכאי himself hold that the third-level loaf is impure?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the logic of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's position as reported in the משנה quoted in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's ruling that a third-level loaf is impure.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: He admitted there is no verse for it, so his ruling seems to have no basis.

steps.title: רב's answer: a קל וחומר from a טבול יום
steps.stepSummary: רב explains that there is no verse, but there is a קל וחומר. A טבול יום does not make regular food impure, yet he disqualifies תרומה. So a second-level loaf, which is itself impure even as regular food, should surely make תרומה a third level.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: From the Torah's verses it has no source, but through a קל וחומר it has one. If a טבול יום, who is allowed to touch regular food, still disqualifies תרומה, then a second-level loaf, which is disqualified even as regular food, should surely make תרומה third-level!
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers the question. רבן יוחנן בן זכאי relied on logic, a קל וחומר, instead of a verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The light case is the טבול יום: he does not affect regular food (חולין), yet he does disqualify תרומה. The strict case is a שני loaf: it is itself impure even as חולין, so it should be at least as strong and disqualify תרומה, making it a שלישי. 'No verse' only meant there is no direct verse, not that there is no source at all.

keyTerms.meaning: A logical argument from a lighter case to a stricter one
Someone who immersed today and becomes fully pure only at nightfall
The holy portion given to a כהן

steps.confusionAlert: "מן התורה אין לו" does not mean the rule is only rabbinic. It means there is no direct verse, but a קל וחומר still gives it a source.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav:
From the Torah it has no [source],
but through an a fortiori argument it has one.
If one who immersed that day,
who is permitted with non-sacred food,
disqualifies teruma,
then a loaf of the second degree,
which is disqualified even as non-sacred food,
is it not logical
that it should make a third degree in teruma?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: מִן הַתּוֹרָה אֵין לוֹ, מִדִּין קַל וָחוֹמֶר יֵשׁ לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14 by giving a logical source instead of a verse.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Supplies an alternate source (קל וחומר) in place of a verse.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: No verse means there is no basis at all for calling the loaf impure.
steps.terutzMaskana: There is no direct verse, but a קל וחומר from a טבול יום supports the טומאה.

steps.title: The קל וחומר is refuted: a טבול יום was once an אב הטומאה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא breaks the קל וחומר. A טבול יום is stricter because before immersing he was an אב הטומאה, a main source of impurity. A loaf never had that status.
steps.simpleTranslation: This can be refuted: what about a טבול יום? He is different because he was an אב הטומאה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב's קל וחומר and shows a weak point in it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קל וחומר only works if the 'light' case really is lighter in every way. A טבול יום has one strict feature the loaf lacks: he started as an אב הטומאה. That may be why he can still disqualify תרומה, so we cannot assume a שני loaf can too.

keyTerms.meaning: This can be refuted (the argument has a flaw)
Since it is (pointing to a special feature)

steps.whatToRemember: רב said the third-level loaf comes from a קל וחומר based on a טבול יום. The גמרא refutes it, since a טבול יום was once an אב הטומאה, which makes him stricter than a loaf.

phrases.english: This can be refuted:
What about one who immersed that day?
He is different, since he was a primary source of impurity!
phrases.notes: Before immersing, the טבול יום was himself an אב הטומאה. A loaf never was.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the קל וחומר given in step 15.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The קל וחומר from טבול יום to a שני loaf.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A טבול יום has a strict feature the loaf lacks: he was once an אב הטומאה, so he is not truly the 'lighter' case.

steps.title: Let it be derived from a better source
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the rejection of רב's קל וחומר by opening with 'derive it,' getting ready to point to a source that was never an אב הטומאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting its answer to the last step's rejection. This one word sets up the next move: it is about to name a source we can learn from instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the last step, the קל וחומר from a טבול יום was rejected because a טבול יום was once an אב הטומאה, and a loaf never was. The word תֵּיתֵי signals that the גמרא will not drop the קל וחומר. It will learn it from a case that does not have that extra strictness.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it come, meaning 'derive it' or 'learn it from'
A logical argument: if the lighter case has a rule, the stricter case surely does
Someone who immersed today but must wait for nightfall to be fully pure
A main source of impurity, which can make people and vessels impure

steps.confusionAlert: תֵּיתֵי is not a question here. It is the opening of an answer: 'learn it from this other case.'

phrases.english: Derive this halakha

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 16's rejection of the קל וחומר by starting to offer a different source case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Substituting a better source case for the קל וחומר
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The קל וחומר fails because a טבול יום was once an אב הטומאה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The קל וחומר can still work if it is learned from a case without that extra strictness. The case itself is named in the next words.
